findings.text: R8's thin interface is priced on work that is not done: "it already computes them for crew list, cli.py:2716-2745" holds for the budget verdict (cli.py:2723-2732 emits budget_seconds, budget_overrun, ceiling_overrun) but not for gates -- gates_total, gates_done and current_gate occur nowhere in reckon/ at 93c28dba and only in docs/ui/crew.jsx, so a reader acting on the remedy finds the gate half unstarted rather than merely unsurfaced.

R8 cites the binding rule as docs/AGENTS.md *The SPA renders; it does not derive*, but at 93c28dba that sentence lives only at AGENTS.md:147 (the repository root file) and docs/AGENTS.md contains no such rule, so a reader sent to the cited path finds nothing -- and the root AGENTS.md is not inside the scope the report declares at report.md:8-9.

the I7 absence control does not reproduce: a literal grep for flight.yaml across the declared scope (all seven skills, ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, the AGENTS.md files, docs/ui) returns zero hits, and docs/AGENTS.md:87 -- named as the one prose hit -- is a config-home sentence that never mentions the file. The absence conclusion holds and a positive control does exist inside the package at reckon/flight.py:8, but the control as recorded names a line that does not carry the searched string.

three cited ranges exclude the lines they name: cli.py:2716-2745 is cited for the four fields that sit at cli.py:2711-2715 (report.md:38, :49, :125), reckon-sync/SKILL.md:287 is cited for a mounts.json write whose inline python3 runs at :289 with json.dump at :295 (report.md:58), and sprint-orchestration.md:306 is cited for a script whose name is at :304 (report.md:96). Each lands in the right function or section, so this is citation drift rather than a wrong location, and it is the size of error a reader following a line reference still feels.
